source.notes: Official CISCE specimen paper with answer key in one PDF. Every page footer prints 'ISC (CLASS XI) SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER 2027' (question paper, PDF pages 1-9) or 'ISC (CLASS XI) SPECIMEN ANSWER KEY 2027' (answer key, PDF pages 10-20); examYear=2027 is the examination year the specimen is published for. It is a SPECIMEN, not a past board paper. No paper/set/series code is printed (the subject code appears only in the file name), so those fields are null. Official answers are taken only from the answer key in the same PDF, trimmed to value points. Cognitive-level tags are recorded as printed. 'page' is the physical PDF page of the question text. Maximum 80: Section A Question 1 has sixteen 1-mark subparts ((x)(a) and (x)(b) are separate entries); Section B Questions 2-9 carry 4 marks each; Section C Questions 10-13 carry 8 marks each. Internal choice ('OR') is printed in Questions 3, 6, 7 (B); these alternatives share a choiceGroup. Questions 11 and 12 say 'Answer either subparts (i) and (ii) or (iii) and (iv)': each subpart is its own entry and all four share the question's choiceGroup (the pair (i)+(ii) is the alternative to (iii)+(iv), 8 marks either way), so the checker's per-group maximum under-counts those two questions. The key states that answers in Sections B and C are 'suggestive and not exhaustive'; long answers are trimmed to value points (ending '…' where cut). Images in 1(xiv) and 1(xv) are not reproduced.

questions.text:
Green Honey Ltd. produces organic honey. The company wants to distribute its product across national markets and needs to decide on the channel: selling the product through wholesalers or supplying it directly to retailers. Each intermediary differs in terms of market reach, cost, control over pricing and profit margins.
Assess the suitability of both the channels and recommend the appropriate one to the manufacturer.

officialAnswer.text: Recommendation and justification • Wholesalers This channel of distribution has a wider reach through many retailers and outlets. Since the wholesalers purchase in bulk, this channel might be better for cost efficiency and volume. Green Honey Ltd. would also receive bulk payments in the form of trade advances. The production at the company would be constant as the wholesalers would procure the product in bulk quantity for sale. However, this channel is better for standardised fast moving consumer goods and not for perishable commodities like honey, so it is not recommended for Green Honey Ltd. • Retailers This channel of distribution would allow Green Honey Ltd. a direct interface with the consumers. Given the perishable and time sensitive nature of the commodity, it is recommended that the company adopts this mode to ensure brand equity. Also, this direct dealing with retailers would enable Green Honey Ltd. to control pricing and ensure uniformity. It would also give them a large share in profit. (Candidates are required to assess both the channels of distribution in the context specified in the question and then recommend one. The recommendation must be supported by at least two…

questions.text: Explain the differences between a contract of Insurance and a contract of Assurance.
extractionIssues: Official answer is a table (page 11); cells re-joined row by row from the text layer, checked against the page render.

officialAnswer.text: Basis | Insurance | Assurance. Core Principle: It is a contract of indemnity. | It is a contract of certainty. Primary Objective: It compensates for actual loss. | It pays a pre-determined amount. Nature of Risk: Risk is contingent. | Event is inevitable. Claim Amount: Insured cannot ‘profit’ from the claim. | There is no concept of ‘profit’ as the actual sum is paid. (Candidates are expected to explain the differences on common parameters.)

questions.text: Explain the concepts of insurable risks and non-insurable risks.

officialAnswer.text: (ii) Insurable risks are events that insurance companies can measure, calculate, and cover for a fee, while non-insurable risks are hazards that are too unpredictable, catastrophic, or tied to potential profit and loss, so insurers refuse to cover them. • Pure Risk Only: Such risks involve only a chance of loss or no loss, with zero chance of financial gain. • Measurable and Predictable: Insurers use past data and statistics to figure out how often the event happens and how much it will cost. • Accidental: In such risks, the loss must happen by chance and outside the control of the person insured. • Examples: Some of the examples are damage due to outbreak of fire, theft, car accidents, and health issues. Non-Insurable risks are those potential losses that do not meet the rules required for insurance coverage. Insurance companies reject these claims because they cannot calculate the odds or the potential payout would bankrupt the company. • Speculative Risk: Such risks carry the chance of both loss and profit, such as starting a new business or trading stocks. • Unpredictable or Catastrophic: Events that happen randomly on a massive scale or cannot be tracked are also considered n…

questions.text:
‘Retailers today are no longer confined to a single channel. By integrating physical stores, mobile apps. and online platforms into one seamless system, businesses are transforming the way consumers shop and interact with brands.’
Discuss the above statement by referring to four features of omni-channel that are relevant to the above statement.

officialAnswer.text: • Omnichannel retailing connects online and physical shopping channels into one single, unified experience. Key Features • Unified Customer Data: It centralises customer details, preferences, and purchase history so that every touchpoint (website, app, or in-store) recognises the buyer and personalises their journey. • Real-Time Cross-Channel Inventory: It synchronises stock levels across warehouses and physical locations, so customers and staff can instantly see item availability anywhere. • Flexible Fulfillment and Returns: It also allows shoppers to mix channels through options like Buy Online, Pick Up In-Store (BOPIS) and return online purchases directly to a physical store. Consistent Brand Voice and Experience: It maintains the same pricing, promotions, messaging, and support quality whether a customer interacts via social media, a mobile app, or a brick-and-mortar register. (Candidates are expected to write those four features of omnichannel that justify the statement given in the question.)

questions.text:
‘Maruti Udyog Limited was originally established as a venture between Government of India, which held a majority stake and appointed representatives to its Board of Directors, and Suzuki Motor Corporation of Japan, a foreign private company that contributed capital and brought in modern technology and managerial expertise. The undertaking aimed to make affordable, fuel-efficient cars accessible to Indian public while also operating on sound commercial and profit-driven principles.’
(Source(edited): https://www.marutisuzuki.com)
What type of business undertaking was Maruti Udyog Limited originally? State three of its features.

officialAnswer.text: Maruti Udyog was originally a Joint Sector Undertaking because both the public sector (Government of India) and the private sector (Suzuki Motor Corporation) invested capital and managed it together. Features: • Mixed Ownership: Capital and ownership were shared between the Government of India (Majority shareholder, with board representation) and Suzuki Motor corporation (a private foreign company). • Combined Objectives: It combined a public welfare goal (making affordable fuel-efficient cars accessible to ordinary Indians) with a profit driven, commercially run approach. • Access to foreign technology: The access to foreign technology and expertise with the private foreign partner brought modern technology and managerial know-how that a purely government-run enterprise would not have had. • (Candidates are required to identify the business type and then explain three of its features.)

questions.text:
A partnership firm has been functioning successfully without registration for many years. A dispute has now arisen between partners regarding profit sharing.
Examine the legal limitations that this unregistered partnership firm would face in resolving this dispute and in enforcing its contractual rights.

officialAnswer.text: (i) Under Section 69 of The Partnership Act, a firm would face quite a few practical difficulties in running its operations if it is not registered. The legal limitations that such a firm would face are: • This firm would not be allowed to file a lawsuit in a civil court against any third party to enforce a right arising out of the contract. • Partners of an unregistered firm would not bring any legal action against any other partner(s) of their own firm to enforce the rights mentioned in the Partnership Deed. • When a third party sues the firm, the firm will not be able claim a ‘set off’ or any other proceeding to enforce a contractual right if the value of the claim exceeds ₹100. • Though the partners and the firm have a legal disability to sue others, third parties can still sue an unregistered firm or its partners. (Candidates have to explain the legal limitations that an unregistered partnership firm would face.)

questions.text:
Surbhi is an entrepreneur. She plans to expand her growing business and seeks advice from her legal team. Her legal team suggests registering her business as a company to raise funds and ensure credibility. She has to choose between a private company, offering control and limited members, and a public company, allowing wider capital access but stricter regulations.
If Surbhi wants to balance growth opportunities with decision-making control, how should she evaluate the trade-offs between registering as a private company versus a public company?

officialAnswer.text: (ii) If Surbhi chooses to register it as a private company, then she would exercise better control due to restricted transfer of shares. She can also avoid hostile takeovers. However, this would also limit the growth of the company as the company will have restricted sources of funds. If she chooses to register it as a public company, then it will expand at a large scale due to availability of massive funds. This would also dilute control due to free transferability of shares. Balanced Justification: A private company may be a better choice in the initial stages of expansion, thereby facilitating better control but long-term growth and expansion is possible only with a public company. (Candidates have to discuss both private and public companies and assess their benefits and limitations, suggesting the one that would ensure stability and long-term growth.)

questions.text: How does e-banking facilitate online monetary transactions for a customer?

officialAnswer.text: (i) Utility of E-banking in online money transfers • Elimination of physical barriers: Financial transactions can be performed 24 / 7 from anywhere in the world, eliminating the need to be physically present at the bank. • Electronic Fund Transfer Mechanisms: Funds can be moved from one account to another safely, in a structured manner. • Payment Gateway Integration: Digital payment gateways facilitate transfer of money while shopping on e-commerce sites. • Real Time Account Management: Customers can access their accounts instantly and monitor their finances by checking transaction history, managing standing instructions etc. (Candidates are expected to explain how e-banking facilitates online payments for customers.)

questions.text: State four advantages of mobile banking.

officialAnswer.text: (ii) Advantages of mobile banking • 24 / 7 access: The customers can check balances, view history, and transfer money anytime, day or night, without worrying about branch operating hours. • Saves time: It saves the customers long queues, paperwork, and arduous travel by completing routine banking tasks in seconds. • Remote Management: The customers can handle transactions from anywhere in the world if they have an internet connection. • Real-Time Alerts: The customers receive instant notifications for every transaction, deposit, or withdrawal to spot issues fast which alerts them and keeps them updated with every transaction. • Built-in Security: Mobile banking uses advanced safety tools like multi- factor authentication, data encryption, and fingerprint or facial recognition which prevents breach of personal and confidential information. • Extra Financial Tools: It enables the customers to track their spending, set monthly budgets, pay utility bills, and deposit checks using app features. (Candidates are expected to write any four advantages of mobile banking.)

questions.text:
Ten small-scale local artisans in a village are struggling to sell their handicrafts as middlemen buy their products at very low prices and sell them at high profit margins in the city.
As an NGO member aiming at protecting these small producers from such exploitation, suggest a suitable democratic form of business organisation. Explain three of its features.

officialAnswer.text: Suggested business organisation: Cooperative Society Features • One person can cast one vote. • It is a voluntary association of members. • Registration is compulsory for society. • Once registered, the society attains perpetual existence. • Liability of the members is limited to the extent of capital contributed by them. • The primary goal of a cooperative society is service and not profit. • Surplus achieved by society is distributed as dividend among the members after transferring the required amount to the mandatory statutory reserve fund. (Candidates have to suggest a form of business organisation relevant to the situation and briefly explain any three of its features.)

questions.text:
Cheesy Cheese Ltd is a company that operates a dairy farm with 500 cows. The company has its own processing plant where the milk is pasteurised and converted into cheese and butter. The company owns a fleet of refrigerated trucks and an online mobile application to facilitate direct home delivery.
Identify the three industries in Cheesy Cheese Ltd. Examine the interplay among them.

officialAnswer.text: The types of industries in Cheesy Cheese Ltd. are Primary, Secondary and Tertiary. Interplay among the three types of industries • Primary: Dairy farm involves the extraction and collection of natural produce directly from Nature • Secondary: Milk is pasteurised and converted into cheese and butter, thereby processing raw material into a finished product. • Tertiary: Dairy products are supplied to consumers which involve services that support the primary and secondary sector activities. (Candidates are expected to first identify the three types of industries referred to in the scenario and then explain their interrelationship.)

questions.text: ‘The sole proprietorship is the oldest and simplest form of business, yet it carries the highest personal risk.’ Justify this statement.

officialAnswer.text: (ii) Sole proprietorship refers to the business formed by an individual who contributes a small amount of capital and manages their affairs and bears all risks. Following are the reasons for sole proprietorship being the ‘oldest and simplest form of business’: • Easy Formation: Sole proprietorship business does not involve any major legal formalities. Registration of the business is not compulsory and is economical. In certain cases, a license may be required. • Minimum Government intervention: This business is free from government intervention. Hence, no legal formalities are mandatory. Reasons for it being risky • Unlimited Liability: The business suffers from unlimited liabilities. The proprietor’s personal assets are often brought into business to pay off the liabilities when there is a lack of funds. • Limited Managerial ability: Sole proprietor may not be an expert in all fields. Hence, there is a limited scope of business expansion with their limited capacity in taking decisions and making judgments. (Candidates are expected to justify the important phrases given in the question by writing valid reasons.)

officialAnswer.text: (i) Blockchain adds significant value to supply chain management (SCM) by addressing long-standing challenges such as lack of transparency, inefficiency, and trust issues among stakeholders. These are explained below: 1. Transparency & Traceability • Every transaction is recorded on a decentralised ledger, visible to all authorised participants. • It enables end-to-end tracking of goods from origin to destination. • Example: In food supply chains, blockchain can trace produce back to farms, ensuring authenticity and safety. 2. Enhanced Trust & Security Once a transaction is recorded on the block chain, it cannot be altered or deleted since each block is cryptographically linked to the previous one. 3. Efficiency through Smart Contracts Smart contracts are self-executing agreements coded into the block chain once the preset conditions are met, this removes manual verification and paperwork, speeding up transactions and reducing delays caused by intermediaries. 4. Improved Compliance & Risk Management • Blockchain can monitor conditions like storage temperature or humidity for sensitive goods. • It ensures compliance with regulatory standards and reduces liability risks. questions.text:

‘The shift from physical stores to digital retailing involves more than just moving products online. It fundamentally changes the nature of consumer experience.’
In the context of the above statement, highlight three features of Digital Retailing.

officialAnswer.text: (ii) Features of digital retailing: • Convenience: Digital retailing allows access to the consumers 24 / 7. • Personalisation: Digital retailers use AI-driven algorithms to analyse consumer data and tailor product recommendations, offers and content to each individual preference • Global Reach: Digital retailing provides global reach, thereby making the experience come alive for consumers. • Information Density: Digital retailing provides plenty of information for the consumers, which may not be possible otherwise. • Interactivity: There is two-way communication between the buyer and the seller. • Dynamic Pricing: The price is not fixed always as the algorithm of the digital platforms keep changing the prices on a real time basis. (Candidates are required to write any three features of digital retailing that relate to the statement given in the question.)

questions.text:

officialAnswer.text: (iii) Resources required for successful implementation of e-business. • Technology Infrastructure: Hardware Computers, high-speed networking equipment. ➢ Software & Platforms: E-commerce platforms (like Shopify, WooCommerce), Content Management Systems (CMS) and secure payment gateways. ➢ Telecommunication System: Reliable, high-speed internet connectivity. • Website / Digital Presence: A well-designed, secure, and user-friendly website with comprehensive product information and high-quality images. • Human Resources: Technically qualified personnel, including IT specialists, developers, digital marketers, and customer service staff. • Operational & Support Systems: ➢ Logistics & Shipping: Systems for order fulfilment and inventory management. ➢ Customer Relationship Management (CRM): Software to manage interactions, analytics, and customer support. • Financial & Legal Resources: Adequate capital for development / marketing and compliance with data protection and consumer rights laws. (Candidates are expected to briefly explain any five resources that are required to implement e-business successfully.)

questions.text:

What is a Multistate Cooperative Society?

officialAnswer.text: (ii) A Multistate Cooperative Society (MSCS) is a cooperative business with members and operations operating in more than one Indian state, registered under the central Multi State Cooperative Societies Act. 2002 and regulated by the Central Registrar. Since its area of operation extends beyond a single state, it does not fall under the jurisdiction of any one state Registrar. Examples include IFFCO, KRIBHCO and AMUL.

questions.text:
Mirali Ltd. is a large manufacturing unit that makes ecofriendly jewellery. Due to the high value of machinery and risk of fire, the company insures its factory for ₹50 crores with Protect Insurance Company.
Considering the risk involved in this case, Protect Insurance Company enters into a contract with Super Safe Insurance Company under which Super Safe Insurance Company agrees to cover 70% of any loss incurred by Protect Insurance.
Later, the top management of Mirali Ltd. feels that their factory is under protected and acquires another insurance cover from Safeguard Insurance Company for ₹40 crores.
Eight months later, a major fire outbreak caused a loss of ₹40 crores at the factory premises.
(i) Identify and explain the concepts of insurance evident in the above situation. [4]
(ii) After the loss caused by fire, Mirali Ltd. approached both the insurance companies claimed the fully insured amount of ₹ 50 crores from Protect Insurance Company and ₹40 crores from Safeguard Insurance Company thereby expecting to recover ₹ 90 crores in total against an actual loss of ₹ 40 crores.
Examine whether its claim is valid. Justify your answer by applying the relevant principle of insurance. [2]
(iii) Assess whether Mirali Ltd. is entitled to a recovery of ₹ 40 crores from Safeguard Insurance Company alone. Justify your answer. [2]
extractionIssues: Cognitive tags differ by part ((i) Understand, (ii)/(iii) Evaluate); cognitiveLevel omitted.

officialAnswer.text: (i) Double Insurance and Re-Insurance The arrangement between Protect Insurance and Super Safe Insurance Company is Re-Insurance as the company is transferring a part of its risk to another insurance company to reduce its possible loss. The arrangement between Mirali Ltd. and Safeguard Insurance is called Double Insurance because the same factory is insured with two different insurers for the sam… (ii) The claim of the company is not valid as the Principle of Indemnity is relevant to this situation. It means a promise to compensate for the loss. The objective of every insurance contract is to put the insured in the same financial position after the loss as they were before.
